existing_tips: 'Partir' uses 'être': il est parti. The past participle agrees: elle est partie, ils sont partis.
Rester uses être. Masculine plural subject: restes.
Mettre can express duration: j'ai mis + time means it took me + time.
In modern French, the imperfect subjunctive is replaced by the present subjunctive in all but the mo
Partir uses être: elle est partie. The participle agrees with the feminine subject.
'Il me semble que' = It seems to me that. 'Sembler' uses the same reverse pattern: il me semble, il
'Avoir envie de' = to feel like / to want. J'ai envie d'un café = I feel like having a coffee.
Possession uses 'de': le livre de Marie (Marie's book), la voiture de mon père (my father's car). No
Adjectives with 'nous' and 'vous' forms of être must agree in number: 'nous sommes fatigués' (plural
'Ne...plus de' = no more. Like 'ne...pas de', the article disappears after negative + de: Il n'y a p
Or: 'now/however', introduces a new and often contradictory fact.
Some color adjectives are invariable (never change form): marron, orange, rose (when used for specif
French floors: rez-de-chaussée (ground floor), premier étage (1st floor = US 2nd floor), deuxième ét
In questions, the structure stays the same: tu as + past participle. Intonation rises.
Days of the week: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche. No capitals. 'Le lundi'
'Au restaurant' uses 'au' (à + le). Time markers like 'hier soir' confirm passé composé.
Verbs of motion use 'être' in passé composé: elle est arrivée. The past participle agrees with the s
'Du/de la/des' for partial quantities: 'Je mange du pain' = I eat some bread (not all bread).
'Cet' is used before masculine nouns starting with a vowel or silent 'h': cet homme, cet arbre, cet
Sortir uses être when intransitive: il est sorti.
Futur antérieur with être: sera arrivé. Arriver takes être.
Don't confuse `il y a` (there is) with `il a` (he has) or `il a y` (doesn't exist). The `y` is manda
